name: Tool Schema Validation Errors
description: Demonstrate what happens when tool schemas are incorrect or tool parameters invalid

steps.mock_tool_parameters_schema: {"type":"object","properties":{"username":{"type":"string","description":"Username for the account"},"email":{"type":"string","format":"email","description":"User's email address"},"age":{"type":"integer","minimum":18,"description":"User's age (must be 18 or older)"}},"required":["username", "age"]}

{\"username\":\"JohnDoe123\",\"email\":\.error_message: Validation error: username must be lowercase alphanumeric with underscores only (no uppercase letters)

{\"username\":\"alice_2024\",\"age\":20}.content: User created successfully: alice_2024 (no email provided)

{\"username\":\"charlie\",\"age\":16}.error_message: Validation error: age must be at least 18

steps.content: Create a user with username JohnDoe123, age 20 and email john@example.com

See the validation error? The agent used 'JohnDoe123' with uppercase letters, but the tool requires lowercase alphanumeric only.

Tool schemas enforce constraints. The agent must adjust parameters to meet the requirements. Also tool should specify Name input requirements directly in tool input schema to prevent invalid calls (like it does for Age).
Create user alice_2024, age 20, no email

Success! The user was created without an email.

This demonstrates an important concept: when a parameter is NOT in the 'required' array, the tool accepts calls without it. The 'required' field in the schema defines which parameters are mandatory.
Create user bob_smith with email bob@example.com, age unknown
Agent knew in advance that tool call would fail, so it adjusted and tried to get the required parameter - it asked the user. (In case it did not ask, used model is quite bad)
Explain to me the difference between required and optional parameters.
